consistency.detail: No release artifact was supplied, so its integrity digest could not be re-verified.
The supplied release index verified against itself — its counts add up and its archive-health verdict recomputes from those counts.
The supplied release policy result recomputed cleanly — its rollup verdict follows from its own recorded facts and assertions.
Both a release gate and a release artifact are required to compare their gate verdicts; at least one was not supplied.
Both a release artifact and a release index are required to check inclusion; at least one was not supplied / usable.
The release policy's effective archive verdict + indexed-artifact count match the release index — the policy was evaluated over the same index.

rollup.detail: BUNDLE PASS: every supplied release-evidence stage passed, the stages AGREE with each other, and the chain included an archive-decision stage. A coherent, content-free evidence bundle for handoff.

archive.note: Archive each present stage's content-free output above, plus this bundle, as CI artifacts — they are the release evidence record for this build. This bundle never uploads or promotes them.

nextAction: Archive the bundled content-free stage outputs as CI artifacts alongside this bundle, then proceed with your out-of-band promotion process (this bundle authorizes nothing on its own).
guidance: Wire this as the FINAL step of a release CI job, AFTER `worker:release-gate` → `worker:release-artifact` → `worker:release-index` → `worker:release-policy`: run each stage to a file, hand those files to this bundle, fail the pipeline on exit 4 (a stage failure or a cross-stage inconsistency), surface exit 3 (an advisory concern) for review, and treat exit 2 (an unreadable/indeterminate stage, or no archive-decision stage) as a setup error, not a pass.

Supply the stages you actually produced; an unset stage is not a fault, but a bundle with only a gate/artifact (no index or policy) is `unknown` — a single build's signal is not an end-to-end chain decision. For a certifiable bundle, include at least a release-index or a release-policy result.

Archive the bundled content-free stage outputs — plus this bundle — as CI artifacts; the bundle is a content-free handoff record, not a substitute for the stage outputs themselves or for your storage-side retention, signing, and release-approval processes.

Enforce promotion out of band: this bundle REPORTS whether the evidence chain is coherent, but signing a release, provisioning, and promoting a deployment are operator/CI actions this offline composer never performs.
caveats: This is a RELEASE EVIDENCE CI BUNDLE: it INGESTS whichever of the content-free release-evidence stage outputs (a `pdfxyz.worker-release-gate/1`, `pdfxyz.release-artifact/1`, `pdfxyz.release-index/1`, and/or `pdfxyz.release-policy/1`) a release job produced, RE-VERIFIES their internal + cross-stage consistency, and folds them into ONE handoff result. It is local content-free bundling + consistency checking over evidence — NOT signing, authentication, cloud validation, storage retention ENFORCEMENT, or deployment promotion.

It is offline and READ-ONLY: it makes NO network call, reads NO secret, bucket, or object, RUNS no stage itself, and NEVER deletes, prunes, uploads, promotes, or mutates any artifact, index, policy, object, or deployment. A `pass` authorizes nothing; it only reports that the stages supplied on THIS host were coherent.

It re-verifies the artifact's integrity digest in-process and recomputes each index/policy stage against itself, and it FAILS CLOSED on disagreement: a stage that failed, a tampered artifact/index/policy, or two stages that describe different evidence forces `fail`. A digest re-verification is TAMPER-EVIDENCE over content-free data, NOT a cryptographic signature — there is no signing key and no attested identity.

It emits only bounded enums, small counts, an ISO stamp, and app-authored prose — so it carries no filename, path, object key, bucket, URL, endpoint, region, job/user id, IP, token, raw ref, raw label, commit URL, size, byte, digest, or document content, even from a hostile stage input, and it never echoes an input file path, even on an error.

A `pass` means the stages supplied MET each other and their own gates on THIS host — not that every archived build passed (the stage verdicts report that separately), that any out-of-band concern (real cloud retention, legal hold, signing, provisioning) is resolved, or that a deployment is approved. Those remain operator-owned.
It is not malware scanning, sanitization, authorization, cloud validation, or deletion proof of any request or object, and it deletes, uploads, promotes, or mutates nothing.
